author: Hesychius of Jerusalem
occasion: Preached for the feast of the Presentation of Christ in the Temple, expounding Luke's account of Simeon and Anna. The preacher says time is short, so he will offer a condensed explanation suited to the occasion and the hearers' desire.
argument: Hesychius explains the Gospel account of the Presentation, showing that the Holy Spirit made Simeon a prophet and temple of God, and led him to receive the infant Christ. He interprets Simeon's song as thanksgiving for seeing the Savior prepared for all peoples, and explains that Christ is set for the fall and rise of many, a sign contradicted especially in the cross. He then praises Anna as prophetess, widow, and temple-dweller, and presents her as proclaiming the redemption of Jerusalem to all awaiting it.

outline.move: The preacher introduces the feast and says he must abbreviate his explanation of Simeon and Anna because of the time.
He expounds Simeon's righteousness, the Spirit's indwelling, his coming to the temple, and his song of release and salvation.
He interprets the prophecy that Christ is set for the fall and rise of many and is a sign contradicted, especially through the cross, and explains the sword that pierces Mary's soul.
He praises Anna's prophetic widowhood and temple service, and presents her proclamation of redemption to those awaiting it in Jerusalem.

cast.name: Simeon
cast.who: The righteous and devout man in Jerusalem who received the infant Jesus in the temple.

cast.name: Anna
cast.who: An aged prophetess, daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher, who served in the temple and proclaimed the redemption.

cast.name: Mary
cast.who: The mother of Jesus, to whom Simeon spoke of the sword that would pierce her soul.

cast.name: Joseph
cast.who: Called the father of Jesus in the Gospel account, though the evangelist knows the virginal conception.

cast.name: Jesus
cast.who: The infant Lord presented in the temple, the Savior and light of the nations.

cast.name: Phanuel
cast.who: Anna's father, mentioned in the Gospel account of her lineage.

cast.name: David
cast.who: The prophet and psalmist whose words Hesychius connects with Simeon's song and Anna's proclamation.

cast.name: Cleopas
cast.who: A disciple on the road to Emmaus whose troubled thoughts were revealed by Christ.

cast.name: Mary Magdalene
cast.who: The disciple whose weak reasoning after the crucifixion was revealed when she asked where Jesus had been laid.

cast.name: Peter
cast.who: The apostle who interpreted Isaiah's prophecy of the cornerstone for the churches.

cast.name: Gabriel
cast.who: The angel who announced to the virgin how the conception would occur.

voices.speaker: Simeon
voices.how_marked: Quoted directly from the Gospel and expanded by the preacher

voices.speaker: The Holy Spirit (imagined address to Simeon)

voices.speaker: The evangelist Luke (imagined reply)
voices.how_marked: Introduced as the evangelist defending himself against an objection, saying he has not forgotten his own account, and explaining that the Incarnate One willed Joseph to be called father in order to deceive the enemy lurking against the mystery of salvation

voices.speaker: Peter
voices.how_marked: Quoted from his epistle interpreting Isaiah

voices.speaker: Anna (imagined proclamation)
voices.how_marked: Introduced with a question about what she was saying, followed by the preacher's reconstruction of her words

scripture: The author uses Septuagint book names and Psalm numbering. Psalm references follow the Septuagint numbering, which is usually one behind the Hebrew numbering for Psalms 10–148. Modern citations should give the Hebrew/English Psalm number with a note where it differs from the Septuagint.
uncertain: The precise date of the homily is not stated in the source.
The exact identity of the congregation addressed is not specified beyond being hearers in Jerusalem.
The source text contains some lacunae and uncertain readings, especially in the section on Cleopas.

_unresolved_facts.fix: The source uses "Ἰησοῦν" (accusative), "βρέφος", "παιδίον", "νήπιον", "λυτρωτήν" — not the nominative "Ἰησοῦς". The source forms should include "Ἰησοῦν" or note that Jesus is referred to by epithet, not by name in the nominative.
The source uses "Μαριὰμ" (sections 8, 9) but never "Μαρία". Remove "Μαρία" from source_forms.
The source form is the genitive "Μαγδαληνῆς Μαρίας", not the nominative "Μαγδαληνὴ Μαρία". Correct to "Μαγδαληνῆς Μαρίας" or note the genitive form.

_unresolved_facts.claim: The evangelist Luke (imagined reply): how_marked: 'Introduced as the evangelist defending himself against an objection, saying he has not forgotten his own account, and explaining that the Incarnate One willed Joseph to be called father in order to deceive the enemy lurking against the mystery of salvation'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: «Οὐκ ἐπιλέλησμαι τῶν ἐμαυτοῦ», φησίν· «εἰ γὰρ καὶ λήθην ἐλάμβανον, τὸ Πνεῦμα ἂν ἐμίμνησκεν. Ἀλλ' οὕτω τότε καλεῖσθαι τὸν Ἰωσὴφ ὁ σαρκωθεὶς ἐβούλετο, ὅπως ἀπατηθῇ ὁ ἐνεδρεύων τὸ τῆς σωτηρίας τῆς ἡμετέρας μυστήριον.»
_unresolved_facts.fix: The voice is not clearly 'the evangelist Luke defending himself' but rather the preacher speaking in a prosopopoeia, with φησίν marking direct speech whose speaker is ambiguous. The brief over-identifies the speaker as 'the evangelist Luke' when the text presents it as a voice responding to the preacher's question 'Τίνος χάριν πατέρα τὸν Ἰωσήφ... καλεῖς;' — the speaker could be the evangelist, the Spirit, or the preacher ventriloquizing. Revise to: 'A voice responding to the preacher's objection, possibly the evangelist or the Spirit, saying he has not forgotten his own account...'

_unresolved_facts.claim: The Holy Spirit (imagined address to Simeon): sections ["u01-rem-early"]
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Τίνος αὐτῷ τὸ βρέφος ὅπερ ἠγνόει μηνύσαντος; Ἀλλὰ γὰρ δῆλον τοῦ κατοικοῦντος ἐν αὐτῷ καὶ χρηματίζοντος Πνεύματος καὶ πάντως που πρὸς τὸν Συμεῶνα λέγοντος· «∆ράμε, πρεσβῦτα, δράμε, σπεῦδε ἤδη...»
_unresolved_facts.fix: The Holy Spirit's imagined address to Simeon is in section u01-open (paragraph 5), not u01-rem-early. Correct sections to ["u01-open"].

Simeon is quoted in u01-rem-early (paragraph 6: 'Νῦν ἀπολύεις...') but not directly quoted in u01-open. In u01-open he is discussed and described, but his direct words from the Gospel appear first in u01-rem-early. Correct sections to ["u01-rem-early"] or note that u01-open contains only references to his words, not direct quotation.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Peter: how_marked: 'Quoted from his epistle interpreting Isaiah'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: οὗτος γάρ ἐστι περὶ οὗ Πέτρος ἀναλαβὼν τὴν Ἠσαΐου προφητείαν ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις ἐπέστελλεν
_unresolved_facts.fix: Peter is not directly quoted but paraphrased/interpreted by the preacher. The text says Peter 'took up Isaiah's prophecy and wrote to the churches,' then the preacher quotes Isaiah (with Petrine interpretation woven in), not Peter's exact words. Revise to: 'Paraphrased as the one who applied Isaiah's prophecy to the churches, with the preacher quoting Isaiah under Peter's interpretive authority.'

_unresolved_facts.claim: Anna (imagined proclamation): how_marked: 'Introduced with a question about what she was saying, followed by the preacher's reconstruction of her words'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Τίνα καὶ ποῖα λέγουσα; «Μὴ πλανᾶσθε τῇ σαρκί...»
_unresolved_facts.fix: The brief is mostly accurate but should note the reconstructed words are explicitly marked as what she was saying (λέγουσα), not merely a reconstruction. The preacher presents it as her actual proclamation content. Revise to: 'Introduced with a question about what and which things she was saying, followed by the preacher's presentation of her words as direct proclamation.'
